- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 2–5%.
- When sentiment turns negative (≤0.2) or shows sharp decline, model often underestimates downside risk; add 1–3% buffer to forecast lows.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days) — cap forecast overshoot at +3% above immediate prior peak.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.4–0.6), model exhibits mean-reversion bias — adjust forecast toward historical 30-day mean if deviation > ±2%.
- Forecast horizon 30d often lags true outcome by 1–3 days; shift forecast 1–2 days forward if sentiment is trending upward.
- When sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.8 → -0.2 → +0.6), model misreads momentum — dampen forecast volatility by 15–20% in such regimes.
